intro: The fourth screen read the set about as well as the third (all items 0.94, inferences 0.85) and, for the first time, judged every template: 55 of 64 pass the legibility gate, up from 35. Three of the six redrawn templates now pass (the heavy seesaw, feeding the birds and the jump). The giant fork failed a third time, now read as a rake; with the stealing bird, the lost balloon and six others it is the work list for v0.8.
screen: Contradictions fell from 0.91 to 0.82, and all of the fall is the giant fork: both set pictures with it lost both contradiction items, the fork read as a rake. Every other contradiction in the set, and all 11 in the probes, was caught and explained. Four set items were misread: the fork twice, the stalking cat once (read as fleeing a dog) and the bird stealing a sandwich once (read as a cap).
redrawn: The heavy seesaw, feeding the birds and the jump pass. The lost balloon comes in just under the gate: the reaching is twice hedged as cheering, and three readers noted the balloon is far from the child. The bird stealing a sandwich was read as theft once and missed once, where it overlapped a kite-flyer's shoulder and was taken for a cap. The fork was read as a rake both times.
gate: All 18 templates the third screen had seen only once were screened at least twice; 16 pass. The two that do not, the dog that wants a walk (read as a cat) and the grazing goat (hedged), join the fork, the bird and the balloon. Four templates that passed in v0.6 fall under the gate on their new pictures: the stalking cat (its crouch read as running), the rain coming (a pointer aimed near a ball in a tree or a cat on the fence), the sandbox (the child seen sitting, not building) and waving (hedged).
